history.summary: FLAG: NON-HINDU RECORD (Buddhism) - kept with flag per project policy. 'Buddha Vihar' here is identified as the Theravada Buddhist Temple at Vivek Vihar, Itanagar (established 1992), a pilgrimage centre for Buddhists in the capital, distinct from the hilltop Mahayana Buddhist Gompa. A striking pair of golden guardian lions stands at its entrance; the inner sanctum has a domed ceiling and a serene idol of the Buddha. It celebrates Buddha Purnima and the Sangken water festival with great fervour - the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh graced the Buddha Purnima celebration here on 14 May 2014. AMBIGUITY FLAG: CSV row 48 is 'Gompa Buddhist Temple', so this record is documented as the separate Theravada temple at Vivek Vihar; if 'Buddha Vihar' was intended as the Gompa, rows 47 and 48 would be duplicates needing a merge. Opening hours are not published - verify locally.

name: Buddha Vihar
town_description: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh (since 20 April 1974), at the foothills of the Himalayas in Papum Pare district, identified with Mayapur of the 14th-15th century. It is known for Itafort (the brick fort that gives the city its name), the Buddhist Gompa, the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum, and Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi). The Theravada Buddhist temple at Vivek Vihar is a key Buddhist pilgrimage seat in the city.
